text:
Still foggy and damp out there at midday, and it'll stay gray all afternoon. We're in the mid 40s now and should creep up toward 51 by late in the day. Rain is the slow part. A few sprinkles or light showers can start from about 1 to 3, but they should stay under a tenth of an inch, so the afternoon is mostly a dry window for errands or a walk. The sun sets just after 4:30, so it gets dark early.

The steadier rain holds off until about 7 tonight, peaks around 10 or 11, and winds down by 3 or so. NWS has about a tenth of an inch, but the European model is a lot wetter, so I'd bet on a bit more than that. It's a cold rain, with a low near 37.

Sunday starts with a few leftover showers until about 9, then stays cloudy and drier, with a high around 50 to 53. Some sun is possible late. Showers return after 7 Sunday evening. Keep the umbrella by the door tonight.

  1. A cooler and unsettled pattern is expected this weekend with summit level snow possible Sunday morning.
  2. Another round of precipitation expected for the start of the work week, with this activity more focused in the favored upslope areas of the northern mountains.
  3. Remaining unsettled midweek through the end of the week, likely trending cooler by next weekend.

AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: We await the arrival of showers this morning as a closed upper low slowly pivots eastward across the central/eastern Great Lakes. Scattered to numerous showers can already be seen out ahead of this feature. This area of showers will continue to slowly drift east-northeastward as its parent low crosses into southern NY, eventually pivoting into our southern sections along a weak inverted surface trough. This band of showers will rotate over NY through this afternoon before shifting east into VT late today and overnight as the upper low spins across southern New England and eventually offshore by Sunday morning. Hence expect fairly widespread showers through the day and into tonight, then becoming more focused in the northern mountains Sunday morning as west-northwest flow develops behind the departing low pressure. Snow levels drop to 2200-3200 ft as the cold pool moves overhead, and expect some slushy snow accumulation will be possible tonight into Sunday morning, generally above 2500 ft. Precipitation will wind down Sunday afternoon, with some sunshine possible by late in the day. Overall rainfall amounts will be a quarter to a half an inch, with locally higher amounts possible in the higher terrain. Temperatures will return to somewhat seasonal normals today and especially Sunday; highs in the 50s today will give way to mid 40s to mid 50s tomorrow. Winds may be a little on the breezy side in the Champlain Valley today as north winds get funneled down the valley. Strong winds then become more widespread on Sunday, though remaining AOB 25 mph or so, with little impact expected. KEY MESSAGE 2: Shortwave ridging briefly builds in behind the departing upper low, giving us a short respite from precipitation. However, another vigorous upper trough will swing along the international border Monday, with another following right in its footsteps on Tuesday. Showers will once again develop, though remaining more focused in the favored upslope areas of the northern Adirondacks/Greens as southwest winds shift to the west and eventually northwest. A reinforcing shot of cold air will see snow levels falling as low as 1500 ft early Tuesday morning, though the bulk of the precipitation will likely have ended by then, limiting potential snow accumulation. Total precipitation amounts will be a quarter of an inch or less through Monday night, with another tenth of two possible on Tuesday. Both days will see temperatures close to or just a bit above normal, generally in the mid 40s to low 50s. KEY MESSAGE 3: The large Hudson Bay low will continue to dominate the weather across our region, bringing multiple shortwaves into the weekend. A Shortwave pushes through on Tuesday bringing valley rain showers and some chances for snow to the upper terrain locations, mainly above 3000 feet AGL. WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - The recent stretch of 60s and even 70s was very pleasant for being outdoors, and it felt like it was September again. However, it’s November, and it’s going to feel a lot more like it in the days to come. Today will start off early with mostly cloudy skies and a few showers, then showers will become more numerous through the day. It will be cooler with highs in the 50s. Showers will continue overnight, then move out from west to east Sunday morning. Up to a half inch of rain is possible, though it looks a touch drier than previously expected. A brief period of snow is still possible in the Northeast Kingdom and Coos County, New Hampshire Sunday morning, though any accumulation now looks confined to the White Mountains with a trace to 3 inches, the highest amounts at the summits. Sunday afternoon will be partly sunny with highs in the 40s. Another system will bring additional rain on Monday, though it will be on the lighter side. Highs will be in the 40s and lows will be in the 30s. A few breaks of sun are possible on Tuesday, but scattered showers are likely, especially north. More widely scattered showers are expected on Veterans Day, though the mountains could get snow showers with colder highs in the upper 30s to low 40s. Dry weather is expected for Thursday and Friday, but temperatures will continue their downward trend. Thursday will be mostly cloudy, and Friday will be partly sunny. Highs will only be in the 30s to low 40s both days, so make sure to have a solid jacket if you head outdoors. Lows will be in the 20s.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-07T13:45:00Z — same caveat): Cloudy and cooler Saturday, showers gradually fill in — This weekend turns much cooler and unsettled, an an upper-level low brings the return of more seasonable air for early November. Saturday will feature a mainly cloudy sky, highs in the low 50s and a stiff north breeze. Scattered showers arrive first in New York, gradually spreading east during the afternoon and evening. Tonight stays cloudy, with passing rain showers and lows in the 30s to near 40. Mountain snowflakes, and a light accumulation, are possible for northern summits (especially in New Hampshire). Sunday looks drier, with morning clouds giving way to a window of afternoon sun — which may illuminate a light dusting of summit snow. Highs will be near 50. Early next week looks seasonably cool, with several chances for rain showers and minor mountain snow accumulations between Monday and Veterans Day. Highs reach the 40s to around 50. Drier weather looks to return by Thursday and Friday. However, expect lots of clouds and chillier temperatures. Highs will be near 40.
